source: Wikidata cast lists for Korean titles that reached a Netflix country chart, joined to Wikimedia pageviews in four Southeast Asian editions
unit: Reads per million reads of the whole language edition, summed across Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia, 12 months. One row is one actor.
question: Does having more charting titles mean an actor's own name is looked up more?
finding: The median actor with five or more charting titles is looked up 9.9 times as often as the median actor with one. The four bands run 1.21, 2.15, 4.72, 11.94 and do not turn back.
whatChangedSince76: We measured this once before with a different instrument and could not read it. That piece asked how far an actor's titles travelled, and for half the panel that figure was a fact about one title rather than about the person. This asks a narrower question — how often the person's own article is opened — and that one moves.
cannotAnswer: This cannot say which way the arrow points. An actor with five charting titles is looked up more, but casting follows attention as readily as attention follows casting, and nothing here separates the two. It is also a floor: readers in these four countries use the English Wikipedia too, and that cannot be split by country.
panelCaveat: This is not every Korean celebrity. It is the cast of Korean titles that reached a Netflix country chart, which is the panel the rest of our data is built on. A singer or idol who never appeared in one of those titles is not here.
